LANDED 172ab21f1 (2026-09-02; refuter BLOCK OVERTURNED by the
coordinator's own clean measurement -- the block rested on a failed
macOS sed that left its 'LIFO' build identical to FIFO, so it saw 0
movers everywhere at base and misread head's real residues as
regressions; distinct-md5 binaries prove the truth below).

GROUND TRUTH (coordinator-measured, both flips verified by md5):
base 910a023f2 -> head 172ab21f1, FIFO-vs-LIFO backend canon:
enum_map_family 1170 -> 0 (CLOSES), 00277 562 -> 562 (unchanged
residue), dead_closure 2 -> 2 (unchanged residue). The builder's
report was exact.

FIX: canonical Types::cmp_tys order on first_class_edges (and the
direct callable_flow_edges_for_targets set) INSIDE
callable_flow_resolution_edges_product, before mint/members/selection
derive -- one canonical order to everything, mint order included; the
body_id weld (transport.rs positional members/selection) forbids
post-hoc reorder, so the sort is at assembly. SECOND leak folded
(refuter-confirmed sound, positional zip at all 3 call sites):
surface_shapes re-sorted rows by mint-order ShapeId while callers zip
positionally -> a boundary carried mismatched shapes (args=[int] but
inputs=[binary], RawInt vs ValueRef); removal restores the
correspondence (latent boundary-content correctness fix, present at
base FIFO, no live symptom found -- codegen tolerated it).

fz-kdt.141 COEXISTENCE (proven): its perturbation wraps the product
DOWNSTREAM of the sort, so wrappers:<seed> permutes the canonical
order and its gate still lands on a moved artifact -- 9/9 stress green.

RESIDUES deliberately NOT forced: 00277 (kdt.107 dispatch-twin class +
a cmp_tys FREE-VAR TIE whose TypeVarId-mint fallback is itself
schedule-visible = fz-kdt.161, filed with the schedule-stable-key fix
direction); dead_closure (kdt.120 return-precision). Both
behavior-identical 3 doors both schedules. Stale census comment in
canon_test.rs corrected (enum_map_family removed from the 'still move'
list, now stated closed; the two survivors named with their tickets).
Gate: lib 1577/0/5, cli 24/0, matrix 476/0/9, clippy/fmt clean,
141 stress 9/9. THE SCHEDULE-AUTHORSHIP CRACKDOWN'S LAST BIG ARTIFACT
GAP IS CLOSED.

comments.text: RIDER (fz-kdt.106 landed, a010532e8, 2026-09-01): 106 changes this ticket's input -- re-measure the callable-flow edge population (was 18 edges) on the post-106 base before scoping; dominance absorption alters which correlated rows exist at the callable-flow surfaces.

COLD-REVIEW FINDINGS FOLDED (fz-kdt.107 review, 2026-09-01 at
788c0c21f):

(1) THIS TICKET OWNS enum_map_family's FIFO/LIFO canon gap -- the last
big schedule-visible surface post-kdt.106. 570 of its ~1,504 diff lines
sit under `selection` (this constructor's plan), and the movement is
whole-family BLOCKS across DIFFERENT question classes (FIFO's a0..a2
rows appear at LIFO's a3..a5) -- cross-class EDGE ORDER, not
within-class arm order. A within-class canonicalization is a measured
no-op on it (option C changed its canon by 0 lines).

(2) DIRECT CANONICALIZATION OF THE PLAN IS IMPOSSIBLE BY CONSTRUCTION
(verified by panic): pattern_dispatch_from_source requires monotonically
increasing body_id (SourcePattern(NonMonotonicBodyId)), and body_id
simultaneously indexes the parallel CallableConstructionFact.members
list -- row order and body numbering are welded. The sound fix is a
canonical order on flow.first_class_edges UPSTREAM
(jobs/runtime_demand.rs:~1155), BEFORE both members and selection are
derived, so there is one ordering authority and everything downstream
inherits it.

(3) The drop half of this ticket (18 droppable edges) inherits
fz-kdt.118's soundness question (observable-surface containment across
fun_top-erased closure positions) -- sequence after 118's verdict.

fz-kdt.141 establishes and exercises this ticket's prescribed ordering point.

Your finding (2) said the sound fix is a canonical order on flow.first_class_edges UPSTREAM (jobs/runtime_demand.rs), BEFORE both members and selection derive, because pattern_dispatch_from_source requires monotonically increasing body_id and body_id simultaneously indexes CallableConstructionFact.members. That is exactly where the wrapper stress reorders now: dispatch_stress::perturbed_construction_members wraps callable_flow_resolution_edges_product's result, so members, the selection plan, boundary_resolution_symbols_for_flow_surfaces and the flow's resolutions list all inherit one order and the weld never has to be broken. No consumer needed changing; the point works.

Corpus evidence that the point is live and reaches everything: 19 fixtures' backend canon moves under a wrappers: seed (00183, 00197, 00230, 00276, 00277, 00391, 00418, 00419, 00420, dispatch_seat_element_blind, enum_hof_three_distinct_closures, enum_map_family, enum_predicate_search, enum_take_drop_split, fz_f98_range_map_converges, list_literal_trailing_call, map_enumerable, opaque_fn_mixed_return, unused_range_binding), and the moved lines include the selection plan's own test nodes. stdout and exit are invariant on all three doors, so this ticket's 'find a fixture where the FLOW plan order alone changes behavior, or prove none exists' now has a measured answer for BEHAVIOR: none exists in the corpus at 584 fixtures x 6 wrapper settings x 3 doors. It is NOT artifact hygiene, though -- see fz-kdt.147: the order decides the whole surface-membership escape population (268 -> 68 -> 20), so the ordering authority this ticket asks for has a real objective to be chosen against.

fz-kdt.132 ripple (2026-09-02): fz-kdt.147 is RETIRED — the 268-escape census its quality-dimension note was built on is EMPTY under every legal wrapper order (the order only ever chose which uncovering member took values; coverage is now correct by construction). This ticket's canonical-edge-order fix therefore has NO escape-minimization dimension left: the goal is pure schedule CONFLUENCE again (enum_map_family's 1170-line FIFO/LIFO gap, the last big one), and any deterministic canonical order on flow.first_class_edges upstream of the members/selection weld suffices. Pick the simplest sound key (cmp_ty-based, per the kdt.101/129 instruments).

fz-kdt.194 landed (04a10fb51): the canonical tie-break for separated arm pairs also fires on construction-wrapper member selection (fz-kdt.179 routed members through the same seat), and it strictly REDUCES your monotonicity violations rather than adding any -- measured 20 -> 6, 202 -> 192, 212 -> 198, and 234/234 unchanged at settled. Worth knowing because your gate runs only where the repair never fires, so that concordance is now measured rather than assumed. The two keys are stated explicitly at the seam: the observable envelope versus surface_inputs.
